Jordan — high-level findings and concrete asks (short form):

1) Key risks: vendor’s LoL and SLA drafts leave Acme exposed to (a) credits-only remedies for repeated outages, (b) broad exclusion of consequential damages that would bar recovery for regulatory fines/data-loss-related third-party claims, and (c) weak operational/exit protections (no escrow/exports, no RTO/RPO, no step‑in/termination for repeated breaches).  
2) Limitation redline (propose): limit overall cap to the greater of (i) 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months or $2M, but expressly carve out and make uncapped vendor liability for (A) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (B) death/personal injury; (C) vendor breach of Data Protection obligations (including regulatory fines and statutory penalties and third‑party claims arising from vendor’s acts/omissions); and (D) IP indemnity — sample: “Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Vendor’s liability for Losses arising from (i) Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of Data Protection Section [x] (including regulatory fines and third‑party claims), (iii) Vendor’s IP infringement obligations, and (iv) death or bodily injury, shall be uncapped.”  
3) SLA/service‑credit & remedies redline (propose): require 99.95% monthly uptime for Production workflows in SOW #1; cumulative credits (sliding scale up to 50% of monthly service fees for severe outages) and credits are supplemental to other remedies; require RCC/RCAs within 72 hours and a remediation plan; permit Acme to terminate for material breach after two consecutive months or four months in any six‑month period of missed SLA with pro rata refund and transition assistance — sample: “If Vendor fails to achieve the Service Availability for two (2) consecutive months or four (4) months in any six (6) month period, Acme may terminate the affected SOW for cause and receive a pro rata refund of prepaid fees and Transition Services.”  
4) Operational protections (propose): add mandatory RTO = 4 hours and RPO = 1 hour for Production workflows; require daily encrypted backups, quarterly security audits/attestation, vendor cooperation in regulatory inquiries within 48 hours, and data escrow/export rights on termination; add step‑in/temporary resources clause (vendor must provide additional engineering resources within 48 hours if outages persist).  
5) Negotiation priorities & next step: make Data Protection carve‑outs and termination-for-repeated-failures non‑negotiable; be willing to accept the cap formula (3x prior year fees) if carve‑outs are included and SLA numbers/termination triggers and RTO/RPO are accepted. If you approve, I’ll produce tracked redlines of §9 and §4.2–4.5 and SOW §3 for the next send.

Jordan — ranked must‑fixs and final redlines (concise):

1) Must‑fixs (ranked): (a) indemnity/Liability alignment — Acme must be able to recover documented regulatory‑response and remediation costs causally attributable to Vendor (vendor’s 12‑month cap currently would bar real world recovery); (b) incident/forensic access — timelines for notice, preservation and access to raw logs/forensics must be concrete and enforceable; (c) BCDR/transition mechanics — RTO/RPO, backups, escrow and staffed transition/step‑in support must be binding with short timelines; (d) SLA/termination triggers — credits alone are insufficient for repeated outages without a clear right to terminate and obtain transition/repairs; (e) audit rights — Acme needs defined third‑party audit and on‑site rights on regulatory notice/material incident.  
2) Liability/Indemnity redline (keeps vendor’s 12‑month structure but carves needed protections): “Notwithstanding Section 9 or Section 10, Vendor shall reimburse Acme for all reasonable, documented remediation and regulatory‑response costs (including required notifications, forensic/legal fees and mandated remediation) incurred as a direct result of Vendor’s breach of its Data Protection or Security obligations (Exhibits D/E). Such reimbursement shall be payable outside the monetary limitation up to an aggregate cap equal to 18 months’ Fees under the affected SOW; provided that Vendor’s liability for (i) Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct and (ii) Vendor’s indemnity obligations for third‑party IP infringement shall remain uncapped.” Rationale: keeps a predictable cap while preserving Acme’s ability to remediate regulatory exposure and preserves the classic uncapped carve‑outs regulators expect (gross negligence/IP).  
3) Incident/audit redlines (drop‑in language for Exhibits D/E): “Vendor will notify Acme within 24 hours of detection of any incident affecting Acme Data, preserve all relevant logs/evidence, provide an initial mitigation plan within 24 hours and a factual RCA and remedial plan within 72 hours; upon Acme request, Vendor must provide access to raw logs/transactional records within 48 hours and reasonable forensic cooperation (including vendor personnel) to Acme and, where requested, to Acme’s regulators. Acme may require one annual third‑party audit (plus ad‑hoc audits upon regulatory notice or material incident); any refusal or failure to provide logs/forensic access constitutes a material breach.” Rationale: defines enforceable timelines that a regulator will expect.  
4) BCDR/termination/transition redlines (Exhibit F + SOW tie‑ins): “For Production workflows Vendor will maintain RTO ≤4 hours and RPO ≤1 hour, daily encrypted backups, and place escrowed exportable copies of Acme Data on termination; if Vendor fails SLA for two (2) consecutive months or four (4) months in any six (6) month period, Acme may (i) terminate the affected SOW for cause, (ii) receive a pro‑rata refund of prepaid Fees, and (iii) require Vendor to provide staffed Transition Services (remote and on‑site as reasonably requested) for up to 90 days to effect safe hand‑off.” Rationale: gives Acme operational continuity and a regulator‑facing exit path without materially reworking FlowLogic’s BCDR structure.  
5) Negotiation note to Priya (2–3 sentence pitch to include): regulators care about demonstrable cooperation, access and remediation ability more than abstract cap mechanics — we can accept a 12‑month fees cap if FlowLogic agrees to the limited reimbursement carve‑out for documented regulatory/remediation costs (capped at 18 months fees), the 24/72/48h incident/log timelines, RTO/RPO/backup/escrow commitments, third‑party audit rights and the termination/transition triggers above; please confirm whether FlowLogic can accept those concrete operational commitments and the limited financial carve‑out so we can incorporate final language.
